about.title: Indio Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When someone dies because of another person's carelessness, the paperwork arrives before the grief has anywhere to go. Families in Indio know this too well. In 2025, five people lost their lives in traffic collisions here, and public records show the heaviest collision volumes along Monroe Street, Indio Boulevard, Jackson Street and Route 111. California law gives certain relatives a way to seek accountability through a wrongful death claim. A surviving spouse or domestic partner and children generally have first standing; certain dependents and heirs may follow. The claim is civil and moves on its own track, separate from any criminal case prosecutors may pursue. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a public entity is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm; we connect Indio families, free, with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

items.question: The crash happened on Indio Boulevard and the driver is facing charges. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, the two proceed separately. A criminal case is brought by Riverside County prosecutors to address the offense, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action your family brings to recover losses. One does not depend on the outcome of the other, and an attorney can explain how they may overlap in practice.

items.question: How long does our family have to file in California?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death. If a city, county or state agency may share responsibility, the time to act is considerably shorter and involves an administrative claim first. Because of that, it is wise to speak with an attorney early rather than waiting.
